messages:
Sam Chen: FYI I'm starting a cross-team spike to define the minimal runtime/infra metrics we need for per-org dashboards (customer-facing) + noisy-neighbor detection. Goal: ship Q2 dashboard templates and add to console.
Anya Patel: great — do we have a list of customers asking for per-org views? Cc @kevin for enterprise needs.
Kevin Ortiz: Customer A and C explicitly asked. Also want the console to enforce tenant isolation in the UI (no token leakage). We'll need RBAC and masked IDs.
Li Wang: for noisy neighbours we should surface request_queue_length, gpu_util_by_tenant, token_rate_per_tenant, model_fanout and cache_hit_rate. Those are the runtime signals we can actually tie to org-id.
Diane Morales: agree. From infra side add: pod_eviction_count, preemptions, node_cpu_pressure_by_az, network_tx_errors. Useful for automated alerts.
Sam Chen: good list. Can you each paste exact metric names we have now? we'll map to naming convention and fill gaps.
Li Wang: current metric names (prometheus):
```
redwood_runtime_request_queue_length{tenant_id=...}
redwood_runtime_gpu_utilization_percent{instance,tenant_id}
redwood_runtime_token_rate_per_sec{tenant_id,api_key}
redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio{model,tenant_id}
```
Kevin Ortiz: infra metrics:
```
node_pod_evictions_total{node}
node_preemptions_total{node}
node_cpu_pressure_seconds_total{node,condition}
network_transmit_errors_total{device}
```
Frank O'Neill: a couple of implementation constraints:
- tenant_id label cardinality could explode if we naive-export every tenant dimension. We need a cardinality plan.
- sensitive labels (api_key) must never be in Prometheus. Use hashed tenant_id or tenant_group.
Li Wang: agreed on hashing. We can add tenant_group label (small cardinality) and keep per-tenant metrics for top N customers via a separate high-cardinality pipeline (ClickHouse).
Anya Patel: UI/UX ask: console needs a per-org "view" toggle that limits all charts to that org and a rollup for "all customers". Also require an exportable CSV for SLAs.
Diane Morales: for RBAC: only org admins (from our identity service) + support with granted access token can view a specific org's dashboard. We'll need backend filtering at query time.
Kevin Ortiz: two approaches:
1) Use Grafana multi-tenant dashboards with datasource-level filtering and org-scoped API keys.
2) Build console-level query rewriting with enforced tenant selectors (easier for rollout, more control).
Sam Chen: preference for (2) to keep UI consistent and allow canary rollout. We already have query rewriting infra in eng-runtime.
Frank O'Neill: canary concerns: when we rewrite queries, we must not add additional cardinality to main Prometheus. Need to route high-cardinality tenant metrics to the observability pipeline.
observability-bot: New ticket created: https://rwd.atlassian.com/browse/OBS-3212 "Per-org dashboards + tenant isolation" assigned to @Li Wang @Diane Morales.
Anya Patel: owners noted. Next: concrete panels we need for customers (template):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (by model variant) scoped to tenant
- Token consumption rate (requests/sec)
- GPU util and batch_size distribution
- Cache hit rate + prefix cache size
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) + error traces link
- Noisy neighbor indicator (burst token_rate + sustained high_gpu_util)
Sam Chen: noisy neighbor indicator proposal: PromQL example
```promql
(sum by (tenant_id) (rate(redwood_runtime_token_rate_per_sec[5m])) > 100)
  and
(sum by (tenant_id) (avg_over_time(redwood_runtime_gpu_utilization_percent[15m])) > 80)
```
If both true for >10m, mark tenant as noisy. We can surface in console and trigger SRE workflow.
Kevin Ortiz: +1 but add cooldown and exclude scheduled batch jobs — we can tag tenant metadata with workload_type to avoid false positives.
Li Wang: implementation plan:
- Day 1: export missing runtime metrics (token_rate, batch_size_histogram) to prometheus-compatible pipeline (low-cardinality).
- Day 3: add tenant_group label and hashing utility.
- Day 5: create Grafana templates + console wrapper endpoints for query rewriting.
- Day 7: alerting rules + noisy neighbor detection job writing to ticketing system.
Diane Morales: infra tasks: ensure we have read-only per-tenant dashboards (no write access) and add audit logs for who viewed per-org data.
Frank O'Neill: security: encrypt tenant mapping table, ensure hashed ids can't be reversed, review by security before canary.
Sam Chen: action items: @Li implement metrics export (owner), @Diane set RBAC + audit hooks (owner), @Kevin prototype console query rewrite (owner), @Anya design per-org UI + export CSV (owner). I'll sync with legal for data residency asks for some EU customers.
Anya Patel: can we have a simple mock in the console for the demo next Thurs? I can wire up sample data if you give me the API endpoints.
Kevin Ortiz: will push a branch with query rewrite endpoints by EOD tomorrow. Link in thread when ready.
observability-bot: OBS-3212 updated: status -> In Progress.
Sam Chen: thanks all. We'll discuss blockers in Tuesday's sync if anything pops up. :thumbsup:
